claims.text: Compositional variation among the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys alters local chemical short-range order.
Compositional variation among these alloys alters the degree of lattice distortion.
Differences in short-range order and lattice distortion change dislocation nucleation and mobility.
Differences in short-range order and lattice distortion change the activation of deformation twinning.
Changes in dislocation behavior and twinning produce differences in yield strength, work hardening, and failure mode.
Constituent count alone is inadequate to explain the mechanical-property differences.
The compared quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys can all be prepared as equiatomic single-phase FCC microstructures through identical thermomechanical processing.
The controlled comparison will hold processing, strain rate, temperature, grain size, and processing history constant across alloy compositions.
Holding these variables constant is intended to isolate composition-dependent effects from extrinsic processing effects.
At room temperature, slip and deformation twinning are active deformation mechanisms in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The quinary alloy has an optimal balance of short-range order and lattice distortion that impedes dislocation motion while favoring useful deformation modes.
Reduced-constituent alloys have either lower lattice distortion or different local ordering than the quinary alloy.
Those structural differences change the barrier to dislocation glide and the operative plasticity mechanisms.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary alloys will have lower yield strength and reduced work hardening.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the ternary alloys will show still larger reductions in yield strength and work hardening than the quaternary alloys.
The quaternary and ternary alloys may exhibit less pronounced deformation twinning and altered failure behavior relative to the quinary alloy.
The quinary alloy exhibits a high-strength–ductility combination.
Grain-boundary characteristics and trace impurities may also influence the measured mechanical properties.
